column1: # Crypta v1.0.0 QA gate - the Catch2 half of the machine-decidable gate.
# One row per gate. Tab-separated, four fields:
#   id           stable identifier, used on the command line (--gates) and as
#                the log file name
#   filter       Catch2 test-spec passed verbatim as a single argument. A
#                comma-separated list of tags is an OR. If a filter ever stops
#                matching any test case, Catch2 exits non-zero and the gate
#                fails - which is the point: a gate that silently stopped
#                testing anything must not read as a pass.
#   measure      extended regular expression. Non-empty means "run this gate
#                with -s and record every output line matching this pattern as
#                a measurement in the report". Use `-` for none; a gate that
#                only has to pass does not need to be re-run verbosely.
#   description  what the gate proves, in one line, for the report
# Gates that are not Catch2 slices - the build, the shipped formats, the IR
# manifest, pluginval, auval - are implemented directly in qa-gate.sh, because
# they are each a different kind of check rather than a different filter.
# Keep this file in sync with docs/qa-checklist.md Part 1.
# id
bypass
column4: Bypass is click-free and latency-compensated, and the wet chain never goes stale (#87, PR #90)

column1: latency
column4: Reported latency matches the actual path and is stable across engine switches

column1: realtime-safety
column4: No heap allocation on the audio thread, across engines, oversized blocks and long silences

column1: param-sweep
column4: Every parameter at both endpoints: finite, bounded by its own declared range, no step beyond 4x its own slew

column1: state-recall
column4: Parameter and preset recall: save/load round-trip, deterministic migration, foreign-preset rejection

column1: rate-and-block
column4: Sample-rate and block-size sweep: block-size independence, degenerate input, reset semantics, no NaN/Inf

column1: null-tests
column4: Null tests: committed golden renders, bit-exact passthrough paths, gain-staging identities

column1: aliasing
column4: Alias-to-signal budget per voicing and engine

column1: voicing-measured
column4: The voicings measure the way the design brief says they do (measured, not heard - see Part 2)

column1: content
column4: Bundled IRs re-measured from the embedded bytes, and the licence bar holds

column1: editor
column4: Editor: accessible name/role/value on every control, focus order, contrast, scale, meter ballistics

column1: manifest
column4: This manifest still describes the suite: every filter above matches a real tag, every gate id is unique
